description: Follow an Antarctic institute, a water-giving monument and Cambridge's most philosophical lamp post before a former picture palace supplies the finale.
short_description: Polar explorers, fresh water, reality checks and a cinema-shaped finish.
author: Day Tripping Quiz
transport_note: A compact route south and east of the historic centre, starting on Lensfield Road and crossing Parker's Piece.

before_you_go.terrain: Town-centre pavements and pedestrian areas, with occasional uneven paving and busy crossings.
before_you_go.hills: Mostly level, with only gentle street gradients.
before_you_go.steps: No steps are required on the intended route; use nearby dropped kerbs at crossings.
before_you_go.accessibility: The checkpoints are outdoors on public routes. Surfaces, temporary works and crowding can vary, so check local access information if step-free travel is essential.
before_you_go.toilets: Check current council, shopping-centre or museum visitor-facility listings before setting off; opening times can change.
before_you_go.footwear: Comfortable everyday walking shoes should be suitable.
before_you_go.dogs: The outdoor route is suitable for dogs kept under control; check the final venue's current dog policy separately.
before_you_go.pushchairs: Generally suitable for pushchairs, though busy pavements and occasional uneven surfaces may slow progress.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Begin where frozen journeys are remembered beneath a warmer university sky.
stops.Hint_1: Head for Lensfield Road, south-east of the city centre.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the public entrance to the Scott Polar Research Institute.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The museum belongs to the Scott Polar Research Institute, founded in 1920 as a memorial to Captain Robert Falcon Scott and his companions and as a centre for polar research.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From the pavement, note one polar symbol, animal or explorer's name visible on the building.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find a stone guardian of the stream that once carried clean water towards thirsty townspeople.
stops.Hint_2: Look for a freestanding classical monument beside the narrow watercourse.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Hobson's Conduit was completed in 1614 to bring fresh water from Nine Wells into Cambridge. Thomas Hobson, the carrier associated with 'Hobson's choice', helped fund the scheme.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Count the visible faces or openings on the monument without stepping into the road.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Cross the grass to the lone lamp where dreamers are advised to check the world is still there.
stops.Hint_1: Enter Parker's Piece and aim for its central crossing of paths.
stops.Hint_2: Find the ornate cast-iron lamp post known by a philosophical nickname.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Reality Checkpoint is the unofficial name of the lamp post at the centre of Parker's Piece. Several explanations for the nickname circulate, but no single origin has been proved.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Look for the words or markings that turn an ordinary lamp post into a local landmark.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: For the finale, trade the common for a royal name in a building once filled with flickering stars.
stops.Hint_1: Leave Parker's Piece towards St Andrew's Street.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the large pub opposite Emmanuel College whose name still sounds like a cinema.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! This food-serving pub occupies the former Regal cinema, purpose-built in 1937 for the ABC chain. Its opening programme included the Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers film Swing Time. Check today's hours, then stop for food or a drink if it is open.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From outside, spot one architectural clue that this broad building was designed for crowds.
